specs.value: Two layers: brown core, black outer coat; lighter than typical soils
Contains dormant beneficial bacteria plus their food; activate on contact with water
Planted tanks with CO2, adequate light and fertiliser
Low-tech tanks without CO2 injection, shrimp and nano tanks

fits.fact: The Plants version is meant for planted tanks and expects CO2 (Neo CO2 or a pressurised system), good light and fertiliser
Sellers say it is safe for fish and invertebrates
One seller rates it well for shrimp keeping and says it helps hold pH down in layouts that use pH-raising rocks
The No CO2 version is aimed at low-tech, shrimp and nano tanks
One seller lists it for foreground to background plants such as Anubias nana, Java fern, Cryptocoryne and dwarf baby tears

usage.fact: Use it straight from the bag without rinsing
Put kitchen paper over the soil and fill slowly to limit clouding; the filter clears any remaining haze
Planting is easier while the soil is damp, before the tank is fully filled
Change one third of the water every 3 days after setup, then one third weekly
For the No CO2 version: lay it 5–7 cm deep, change water often in the first 1–2 weeks, and avoid disturbing the substrate afterwards
After 5–6 months, add root tabs/base fertiliser or liquid fertiliser to extend the soil's life
Store unused soil dry and out of direct sun

issues.fact: May contain small impurities such as bits of wood
Coloured bacteria may show up in the bag; the distributor says this is normal
Mixing it with another brand's soil raises the algae risk and calls for more water changes; one seller says not to mix at all
Sellers contradict each other on fertiliser: one page says nothing extra is needed but also tells you to add suitable fertiliser
The versions differ: Compact/Plants Normal is for CO2-injected tanks, while No CO2 is made for low-tech setups
Sellers make claims (pH 6.5–7.5, NPK and trace content) that the manufacturer has not been shown to confirm

alternatives.why: The benchmark premium soil that lowers pH and KH. It costs much more and is more prone to turning muddy
Japanese soil made from volcanic ash in several grain sizes, including Extra Fine for nano tanks. One forum user said it was the only soil that gave them no ammonia spike
A cheaper sibling in the same range (280,000₫ for 3 L) that suits low-tech tanks without CO2
